main_text.l: [Engraving: emblem of Prudence, a two-faced crowned head with scales above, arrows at either side, and a sword-like shaft down to an open book.]

l.i: Prudens te pietas, pia te prudentia stipet, Quisquis es, vt populis iura verenda roges. Tale olim te iudicium, mihi crede, manebit, Quale heic in plebem forte tuere tuam.

page.notes: The engraving is described, not transcribed. The verse is set in italic with a long-s-free transcription; the first line's initial P is a decorated capital. The catchword "Duæ" is printed at the lower right. Some letters in the verse are faint and were read with reasonable confidence.
